title: Average rate of change
parts: The change in position divided by elapsed time.
example: Moving from 2 m to 8 m in 3 s gives an average velocity of 2 m/s.
note: Change is final value minus initial value.
wrong: The elapsed time divided by the change in position.

title: Dimensions of velocity
parts: Velocity has dimensions of length divided by time.
example: Both m/s and km/h have dimensions LT⁻¹.
note: The brackets describe dimensions, and L and T stand for length and time.
wrong: Velocity must be measured in metres per second.

title: Newton’s second law
parts: The net force on a constant-mass object
example: A net force of 12 N on 3 kg gives an acceleration of 4 m/s².
note: Add the forces as vectors before relating them to acceleration.
wrong: The net force equals mass times velocity.

title: Linear model with an error term
parts: Observation i is modelled as an intercept plus slope times input plus an error term.
example: With β₀=3 and β₁=2, input 4 gives a fitted mean of 11. An observed 10 has a residual of −1.
note: β₀ is the model mean at x=0.
wrong: β₁ is the prediction when x is zero.

title: Exponential model
parts: Start at P₀ and multiply by a for each unit increase in t.
note: A fixed multiplier gives a fixed percentage change per unit.
wrong: Add a to P₀ at every time step.

title: Direct proportionality
parts: y is a fixed multiple of x.
example: If y=3x, doubling x doubles y.
note: Adding a nonzero intercept breaks direct proportionality.
wrong: y is proportional to the reciprocal of x.

title: Rate balance
parts: The rate of change of stored mass is inflow rate minus outflow rate.
example: If 7 kg/h enters and 4 kg/h leaves, mass rises at 3 kg/h.
note: Both right-hand terms are rates with the same units.
wrong: Stored mass equals the sum of the two rates.

title: Reynolds number
parts: Density times characteristic speed times length divided by dynamic viscosity.
example: For 1000 kg/m³, 0.1 m/s, 0.01 m and 0.001 Pa·s respectively, Re=1000.
note: The units cancel. The result depends on the chosen characteristic speed and length.
wrong: The result is measured in metres per second.
